137.t: Cavalcade of Jazz with Jack Teagarden
137.s: On a 1947 touring package with Teagarden, Dinah Washington, Lips Page and others, Durham wrote the whole show.
137.ch: Cavalcade, Wynonie Harris and the 1953 show
137.q: The singer was Dinah Washington, June Christie, Charley Van Tour, Lee Castle, Red Rodney, Lips Page and Flat Top Wilson. And we had a piano player, African fellow named Freddy Weiss (inaudible).

137.t: How the Cavalcade show was staged and paid
137.s: He wrote openers and closers for each star act; Teagarden got $1,000 a week and the printed magazine sold well at a dollar fifty.
137.ch: Cavalcade, Wynonie Harris and the 1953 show
137.q: Yeah, we was playing concerts. Like, Jack Teagarden would play his trombone and he would do three or four numbers and sing. But I had it fixed so when he played, when he come out, I would have the reed section, because we had George ________ was on that show and Morris Loudon and Charlie Van Tour.…

137.t: The 1953 three-band package show with Little Richard
137.s: He booked and led a theater package with Little Richard's band, his own six-piece and a six-piece girl band, and trouble started when a promoter ran off with deposits.
137.ch: Cavalcade, Wynonie Harris and the 1953 show
137.q: Well, I organized the show. I think (inaudible) nine years, went on down into Richmond, Norfolk, Newport, Georgia. Within that show, I had three bands traveling and Little Richard's band (inaudible) five-piece band and I had my band, which was six pieces, boys, and had a six-piece girl band.

137.t: Dancers, singers and the backers of the show
137.s: The show added dancers and singers including the Durmettes, with backing from a wealthy family, and he bought the Dominoes' station wagon.
137.ch: Cavalcade, Wynonie Harris and the 1953 show
137.q: No, some other girl. And then I had another girl called -- the girl that looked just like Lena Horne. She was with Muhamma (inaudible), pretty girl, and she was doing a location over there in Jersey. We got her costume and she was doing the rumba rhythm stuff. I had another girl who sung ballads,…

137.t: Stock cards, theater bookings and how the lawyer ruined it
137.s: The tour did percentage in theaters until his West Indian lawyer took deposit money, so he dropped the show and Little Richard moved on.
137.ch: Cavalcade, Wynonie Harris and the 1953 show
137.q: Yeah, could do it. Everybody was wondering -- Pasadena printed on the cards and he said Gail called him, Evans come down. Everybody wanted to know who's backing the show. Who's got this show out? Because the stock cards was beautiful. I had a group called the Durmettes, organized a group of girls…

167.t: Honolulu with Jack McVey at Don the Beachcomber's
167.s: He went to Honolulu with Jack McVey's show band, with Louise Beavers singing and a rhythm and blues repertoire.
167.q: Of course what's his name would be doing his thing. Jack McVey would be doing his thing, like getting out in the middle of the floor, you know, on top of the bandstand.

167.t: Joining Louis Jordan in Las Vegas and the Bermuda trip
167.s: Bunn worked about two years with Jordan after the war, joining him in Las Vegas from a lounge group.
167.ch: Louis Jordan, Ink Spots and the union
167.q: Yeah. These things come back to you. They're coming back to me, now. Which is wonderful. Things you can't remember, you mention things you know I've been [through], and naturally I own up to it because I remember it.

78.t: Seven-piece band, Bryce Roperson, and trumpeter Gail Brockman
78.s: His Minneapolis-based seven-piece band, with white guitarist Bryce Roperson and trumpeter Gail Brockman who played the Red Top solo with Gene Ammons, joined Billy Williams' revue and went to Las Vegas.
78.ch: Starting out in New York and Chicago
78.q: enough. I used to go down and stand down and watch these things. They said, you want to see guys go upstairs and come out with -- guys used to stand on the street sometime with a trumpet, saxophone, and fiddle. Violin, you know. (Inaudible) Waitin' for -- all gigs in New York. (unintelligible).…

78.t: 1950s: Minneapolis base and the Billy Williams Revue in Las Vegas
78.s: From his Minneapolis Key Club band, Horace joined Billy Williams for the Riviera and Starlight Room in Vegas, six engagements, one of the first revues there, featuring trumpeter Clora Bryant and the Four Dukes.
78.ch: Army band, Lena Horne, Billie Holiday and the 1950s
78.q: Minneapolis was the base -- the jumping off place, I should say, with Billy Williams. Billy Williams brought his Charioteers to this particular Key Club where my band was housed, and he loved this group that I had so much so that he said to me one day, "Hey man, I've got a date in Vegas at the…

653.t: Backing the Famous Flames and Little Richard, and why he quit
653.s: On a Milt Shaw tour his band backed James Brown and Little Richard; he quit over makeup and dress while Charles Connors and Wilbert Smith stayed.
653.ch: On the road and into brass bands
653.q: George. Oh. What the hell was George's name? Anyhow. His professional name was Papa Lightfoot. His real name was George something. I can't remember now. Anyhow. So we traveled like that for quite some time with Senegal and so forth. Then the band changed up. We started doing some gigs for Milt…

654.t: His role as Buddy Rich's assistant drummer and other employers
654.s: Kay corrects the myth that he drove the bus or played the charts; he played acts and vocals, later worked with Frankie Laine, Patti Page and Josephine Baker.
654.q: No. What it was, see it’s a fallacy. People write what they think. They think that I drove the bus, which I never did because I couldn’t ride a bicycle. I didn’t drive any bus. I could drive a car. What it was is I was his assistant so to speak. In other words they said that I went and played the…

565.s: The doomed Vegas show with Tito Rodriguez, his band, the Billy Williams Revue and Horace Henderson, and getting fired.
565.ch: Sideman years and early band leading
565.q: Oh God, one of the biggest names. But he wanted to do a show. And then, his wife was Japanese, that he had met in the China Doll... He wanted to do like a Lucille Ball-Desi Arnaz. That’s how Desi met Lucille Ball, and they became so popular in the ‘50s with their show. Tito Rodríguez saw himself…

406.t: Murray Wanger's Cotton Club revue in Miami and Cab's disastrous rehearsals
406.s: Manager Murray Wanger wanted to recreate a Cotton Club show in Miami. Barefield assembled the band and wrote the music, then conducted opening night when Cab was disgusted by the confusion, and the show was a hit.
406.ch: Streetcar, Cab revival shows and trips abroad
406.q: And then in '57 Cab -- this -- let's see, how was that? Oh, Murray Wanger, do you know that name? Well, he was the man that -- that managed Mae West, managed a lot of big movie stars. This guy, he was a marvelous manager, and he made three or four fortunes in managing. And he was a spender. He was…

88.s: A Pullman-car show with Nat and Perry Como played five stadiums before 35,000-40,000 people.
88.q: So I made -- then Nat went out with another show; we took a big show out with Pullman cars -- it was Nat Cole and Perry Como, and Perry was big on television then. And on that show it was Perry Como and Nat Cole, Roy Hamilton, Ralph Marterie band, Peg Leg Bates, Sarah Vaughn, and a cast of…

452.t: Rebuilding the band and a package show with Dinah Washington
452.s: After recovery Cobb re-forms his band without Booty Wood and Charlie Fowlkes and goes out with Lamar Wright Jr. on a Dinah Washington package show booked by Universal.
452.ch: On the road, James Brown and the 1956 crash
452.q: Well, on that first time I got everybody back, but the second time I did not because Charlie Forbes had gone with Basie, and he stayed there. Bootie didn't come back. I got Dickie Harris Arriage. George Rhodes Rule came back. I had another bass player, another drummer, Al Jones out of Philadelphia.…

93.t: Robinson's tour with Don Redmond's show
93.s: Green introduces the story: Robinson in Shirley Temple films, then a personal appearance tour with Don Redmond's orchestra, Peg Leg Bates and Chuck and Chuckles at Boston's RKO Palace.
93.ch: Bill Robinson and Chuck and Chuckles
93.q: Well, once upon a time, as time came on or came by or passed, he eventually got into moving pictures with Shirley Temple, the child actress star. He used to teach her. He used to do choreography for him and her. And he called it terpsichore, he said, and he would make up these dance routines, tap…

19.t: The Biggest Show of 1952 with Nat Cole, Stan Kenton and Sarah Vaughan
19.s: Touring with Cole's trio and Kenton's five-section band, he meets Kenton sidemen like Stan Levey and Conte Candoli.
19.ch: Washington clubs, Louis Jordan and Sarah Vaughan, 1949-54
19.q: In the fall of 1952, there was a show that had gone out the year before, and it was called The Biggest Show of 1951. That show featured Duke Ellington's band, Sarah Vaughan, George Kirby, an act called Stump and Stumpy, Peg Leg Bates, a lot of other people that I don't remember -- but that show had…

239.t: The Big Show of 1951: Sarah, Nat King Cole and closing spots
239.s: On the first big package show, with the Ellington band, George Treadwell made Sarah late to test her closing slot, and Nat Cole proved the heavyweight.
239.q: And then we can start the second half of the show. And there was another time, in what we called the Big Show of '51, which was the first big package show, this was with the Ellington Band. Oh, we had the Marie Bryant Dancers and Peg Leg Bates, Stumpy and Stumpy, Patterson and Jackson, Jimmy…
